land.text: Pernambuco, whose independence Manuel Paes de Andrade 'announced' on 2 July 1824

predecessors.note: The infobox location is Pernambuco, Ceará and Paraíba; the page says only "a few villages in southern Ceará and in Paraíba" adhered.

land.text: Pernambuco, retaken after the attack on Recife of 12 September 1824 and the defeat at Olinda five days later

successors.note: Frei Caneca was executed on 13 January 1825, after the end.

capitals.name: Recife
capitals.note: Infobox caption "Recife, capital of the Pernambuco province, 1824"; the page lists no capital for the Confederation itself.

correction.text: Pernambuco, where 'Manuel Paes de Andrade ... announced the independence of Pernambuco' on 2 July 1824; infobox location Pernambuco, Ceará, Paraíba

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, Cliopatria has no row. The page says that of the provinces invited (Grand Pará, Maranhão, Piauí, Ceará, Rio Grande do Norte, Alagoas, Sergipe, Paraíba, Pernambuco, Bahia) 'none of them adhered ... with the exception of a few villages in southern Ceará and in Paraíba', so the shape is Pernambuco alone. No area on the page.

ledger.note: 2 July 1824: Manuel Paes de Andrade proclaims the Confederation of the Equator at Recife. 'On July 2, 1824, only one day after the departure of Taylor, Manuel Paes de Andrade ... announced the independence of Pernambuco.' The page names the province, not its limits.

region.text: Pernambuco, after the army 'attacked Recife' on 12 September and the rebels were defeated 'five days later in Olinda'

ledger.note: September 1824: the Confederation is crushed. 'On September 12, the army led by Brigadier General Lima e Silva and Paes Barreto attacked Recife'; the rebels were defeated 'five days later in Olinda' (about 17 September). Cochrane, sent on 2 August 1824, was 'already blockading Recife'.
September 1824: the rebel state ends. Infobox 'Result: Loyalist victory'; Frei Caneca was executed on 13 January 1825.

wars.name: Confederation of the Equator

zones.text: Pernambuco, blockaded by sea from April and August 1824 and attacked on land on 12 September

wars.outcome: Loyalist victory: Recife attacked on 12 September 1824, the rebels defeated at Olinda five days later; Frei Caneca executed 13 January 1825.
wars.note: The page has John Taylor's blockade in April 1824 and Cochrane's from August 1824; no other province joined.

certainty.note: Only the province of Pernambuco is named; its limits are not described.

sources.title: Confederation of the Equator
sources.note: Proclamation 2 July 1824; provinces invited and refusing; blockade; attack on Recife 12 September; Olinda five days later; Frei Caneca 13 January 1825.

notes:
Cliopatria has no row. The empire-of-brazil dossier (am-08-b) records the contest with counterpart 'Confederation of the Equator' (2 July to September 1824) around Olinda; this is its dossier, type rebel (rule 5).
One page opened (budget 1-2). The page does not mention a constitution of the Confederation and only says that 'a few villages in southern Ceará and in Paraíba' adhered: a gap-filler may add Ceará and Paraíba if a page dates their adherence. The Olinda date is 'five days later' than 12 September, i.e. about 17 September.
